b5_20day_tradable_entry_by_liquidity.definition: 424B5 shelf takedown, SHORT entered at the close of F+1 (the first session on which the filing is unambiguously public), held 20 sessions, IWM-hedged. Sign convention here is the RAW long return, so negative = the short makes money.
b5_20day_tradable_entry_by_liquidity.verdict: NOT PROMOTABLE. Design t = -1.96 is below the 3.01 two-sided within-theme bar and far below the 3.28 pooled bar, so the held-out -3.85 is selection on the held-out. And the whole effect is confined to $2-20M ADV microcaps: it is exactly zero in every liquid bucket in BOTH windows. A microcap short is where borrow cost and borrow availability bind, and neither is in this data.

verdict.one_line: The mandated flow is real and enormous -- a median $4.3bn print at 29.7x normal volume on an S&P 500 add's rebalance close -- and it is completely pre-priced: on the day it executes the price moves +0.02% (t=0.49). Every tradable formula died.

only_design_survivors_and_why_they_died.F37_PROMOTE_REB5: design t +3.09 (positive in all six design years) -> HELD-OUT t -1.12. Dead. Its own mechanism decomposition (block 4) had already contradicted it.
only_design_survivors_and_why_they_died.F27_SEC424B5_REB5: design t -5.86 -> held-out t -5.48, confirmed. Then killed by the timing control: the entire effect is the F->F+1 day and the filing-day return is flat (-0.09%, t -0.63), i.e. the filing is disseminated after the close and entering at the F close is a LOOKAHEAD. Entering at the F+1 close earns -0.23% (t -0.80) held-out, and +0.06% (t +0.31) in liquid names.
only_design_survivors_and_why_they_died.F12_SP600ADD_RUNUP5: design t +7.45 -> held-out t +7.87. Real, replicated, and untradable: 96% of the move is one announcement-day jump, and from the announcement close onward the return is -0.28% (t -0.83).
